question: X can do a job in 20 days, Y in 30 days and Z in 36 days. Y and Z begin the work but have to leave after 5 days. How many complete number of days will X take to finish the remaining job?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(20, 30, 36) = 180 units

Efficiency: X = 9, Y = 6, Z = 5

Work done by Y and Z in 5 days = (6 + 5) × 5 = 55 units

Remaining work = 180 − 55 = 125 units

Days taken by X = 125 ÷ 9 = 13.88 ≈ 14 days

**∴ The correct answer is 14 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by X = 20 days

Time taken by Y = 30 days

Time taken by Z = 36 days

Y and Z start the work and leave after 5 days.

**Method Used:**

We will use the LCM method to find the total work and the individual efficiencies.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 X

 Y

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work = LCM(20, 30, 36) = 180 units.

⇒ Efficiency of Y and Z working together = 6 + 5 = 11 units/day.

⇒ Work done by Y and Z in 5 days = 11 × 5 = 55 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 180 − 55 = 125 units.

⇒ Time taken by X to complete the remaining work = Remaining work ÷ Efficiency of X

⇒ Time taken by X = 125 ÷ 9 = 13.88 days.

⇒ Since 13 whole days will only cover 117 units of work, X will need an additional part of the 14th day to finish the remaining 8 units.

⇒ Thus, the number of complete days needed to fully finish the job is 14 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Approach

Total work is generally considered as the LCM of the time taken by each individual. Efficiency is then calculated as Total Work ÷ Time taken.

Pipes and Cisterns

This concept works on the identical principle of Time & Work. The only variation is that an outlet pipe or a leak performs negative work as it empties the tank.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual amount of work done by each person. If everyone works for the same number of days, the wages can be distributed directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.
